method.nativeInspection: Blender 5.2.1 background read of the pinned V8 .blend; bounds are object matrix_world applied to native mesh vertices, in Blender XYZ metres. No scene save or render.
method.visualInspection: Existing neutral authoring side-left still only; visual attribution is not a pixel-level ownership segmentation.
method.runtimeCoordinates: Native bounds use Blender axes. Exported GLB coordinates are converted by (x,y,z)_glb=(x,z,-y)_Blender.

rig.runtimeBehavior: era-motion.js bends the neck and counter-rotates the skull at fixed length for strike/contact; it does not translate or stretch the neck to reach.

interpretation.visualAttribution: The dominant tall angular outline is the paired Bowed passive cervical fork meshes; the broad inner frame behind/between them is Cervical articulated inner guards. The six throat laminae form a central anterior cascade but do not close the side opening shown in builder-side-left.png. The inventory has no neck-region bearing-role mesh; the joint controls are the neck/head empties.
interpretation.coordinateAudit: The older six-guard study's neck_surface produces world-space points and explicitly transforms them through neck.matrix_world.inverted() before parenting under neck with identity parent inverse/basis. This correctly cancels the neck pivot's -0.1 m Y offset. The proposed ~100 mm aft-placement error is not supported by that code path. Its section centers match the authored stations in alignment-v6-neck.py; however, its piecewise-smoothstep sampling, narrow side-only angular span, and three separated bands do not create a broad continuous curved outer neck. Its earlier failed clearances therefore do not by themselves prove a pivot change is needed.
interpretation.referenceBoundary: Candidate03 supports a fuller curved neck-to-breast exterior only qualitatively. It gives no measurable dimensions, hidden-side topology, fork/bearing design, or pivot hierarchy. The current six-plate cascade, forks, inner guards, and any suggested additional construction remain authored proposal geometry rather than reference-measured mechanism.
options: First evaluate a broader curved set of rigid, overlapping exterior plates spanning the neck-to-breast silhouette, attached to the existing neck owner so they follow the current fixed-length articulation. This is the smallest structural change and must be checked against head, jaw, breast/fixings and runtime poses.

If plate coverage cannot remain coherent under the existing neck bend, consider a revised articulated neck/head hierarchy or additional neck sub-pivots. The original geometry contract does not make all 51 pivots sacred, but any hierarchy change affects motion, fixed-length contact, inspection/restoration, export matrices and all pose clearances; no evidence here establishes it is necessary.
limits: Bounds are exact per native object at rest; no pose-specific clearance was measured in this diagnosis.
The side image has no ownership colors; attribution is corroborated by the exact native object set and bounds but not pixel-segmented.
No collision, articulation durability, owner acceptance, or final-art claim.
